MARKET.head: California Table Grape Commission hires Suzanne Devereaux-McKinstrie for North American marketing
MARKET.summ: The California Table Grape Commission has added Suzanne Devereaux-McKinstrie as its Global Marketing Director for Canada, Mexico, and Central America
takeaways: The California Table Grape Commission has named Suzanne Devereaux-McKinstrie its Global Marketing Director for Canada, Mexico and Central America.
She was previously chief executive of the Center for Produce Safety and international marketing director for American Pistachio Growers.
Her role is to grow demand for fresh California table grapes through importers, retailers and in-market representatives.

MARKET.head: Bone Dry returns as wine partner for 40th ARIA Awards in Sydney
MARKET.summ: South Australian wine label, Bone Dry, will be the official wine partner of the 2026 ARIA Awards in partnership with Spotify, as the event marks its 40th anniversary in Sydney tonight. Part of the family-owned Australian CW Wines portfolio, Bone Dry returns after its debut as wine sponsor in 2025. Bone Dry will be the primary...
takeaways: Bone Dry, a South Australian wine label owned by family-run CW Wines, is official wine partner of the 2026 ARIA Awards.
The partnership runs with Spotify, marking the Sydney music awards' 40th anniversary, and Bone Dry returns after sponsoring in 2025.
Bone Dry is the primary wine served on the night, alongside Reschke and Fourth Hill, both CW Wines brands.

MARKET.head: Wine Australia opens funding call for innovative grape and wine projects
MARKET.summ: Wine Australia is today launching a competitive call for innovative eligible projects to secure funding from the Research & Innovation Fund (RIF) which is part of the Australian Wine Future Fund (AWFF). The organisation said innovative and groundbreaking projects tackling the wine industry’s most critical challenges will be...
takeaways: Wine Australia launched an expression of interest for its Research & Innovation Fund, open until 23 December 2026.
The Australian Wine Future Fund targets $50 million over five years, mixing Commonwealth, state, partner and private money.
The Research & Innovation Fund aims for $35 million via grants and co-investment, with a $15 million Venture Investments Portfolio alongside.

MARKET.head: Penfolds tops JD.com's Singles' Day wine rankings, with Cloudy Bay and Changyu in top five
MARKET.summ: China’s biggest online shopping season has produced a new set of winners in wine - and while familiar names dominate, a few less obvious brands have broken into the top 10
takeaways: JD.com's Singles' Day rankings put Penfolds first among wine brands, followed by Changyu, Great Wall, DBR Lafite and Cloudy Bay.
JD.com did not say whether its rankings were based on sales value or volume, and alcohol transaction value rose 25% year over year.
Great Wall Five Star Cabernet Sauvignon transaction value rose 72%, while Château Haut-Brion was the only wine on the high-growth list at RMB 1.43 million.

MARKET.head: ProWine Mumbai to showcase India's wine and spirits market to global producers
MARKET.summ: India’s growing appeal to international wine and spirits producers will take center stage at ProWine Mumbai this month, as rising disposable incomes, demand for premium drinks and new trade agreements open opportunities in the market
takeaways: ProWine Mumbai runs November 18-19 at Jio World Convention Centre, expecting 200 exhibitors and 6,000 trade visitors.
India's free trade deals with Australia, the UK and New Zealand, plus a January 2026 EU deal, will cut tariffs on some imported wines and spirits.
The event, co-organized by Messe Düsseldorf India and All Things Nice, includes ProWine Connect matchmaking with importers and distributors.

MARKET.head: Australian white wine shipments to China more than double in Q3 2026
MARKET.summ: White wine export volumes to the market more than doubled, rising 143.6%, according to Wine Australia data. The growth comes as Australian producers seek a greater foothold among Chinese white wine drinkers, including consumers exploring alternatives to Burgundy
takeaways: Australian wine exports to mainland China rose 1.9% by value in Q3 2026, while global exports fell 7.3%.
White wine export volumes to mainland China rose 143.6% in the quarter, to 5.26 million liters, per Wine Australia data.
White wine still made up just 7.14% of Australian wine export value to mainland China, against 91.62% for red.

CULTURE.head: VinePair names 30 wines for Thanksgiving 2026, favoring low-alcohol, high-acid picks
CULTURE.summ: Amid the marathon of planning, prepping, cooking, and baking, finding the perfect wine for Thanksgiving isn’t always the top priority. If wine is on the checklist, venturing into bottle shops this time of year can be especially dizzying and sometimes even stressful. So many choices, so little time to choose, and what’s my budget?
takeaways: VinePair's tasting staff selected 30 Thanksgiving wines for 2026 from bottles reviewed across its buying guides this year.
Selection favours high acidity, lower alcohol and delicate flavours, with Riesling, Cabernet Franc and Pinot Noir frequently recommended.
The list includes value picks, splurges and American wines such as a New York Merlot and a Virginia red blend.

CULTURE.head: Vavasour Awatere Valley Sauvignon Blanc named 2026 Marlborough Wine Show champion
CULTURE.summ: Vavasour Sauvignon Blanc 2026 has been crowned the Champion Wine of the 2026 Marlborough Wine Show, sponsored by QuayConnect. The accolade for the Awatere Valley wine comes 40 years after Vavasour planted the valley’s first vineyard in 1986. “This is an amazing result for our team,” said winemaker Stu Marfell.
takeaways: Vavasour's 2026 Awatere Valley Sauvignon Blanc was named Champion Wine of the 2026 Marlborough Wine Show, marking 40 years since the valley's first Vavasour vineyard in 1986.
Judging was led by chief judge Murray Cook and winemaker Stu Marfell, who tasted more than 500 wines blind with 10 senior and six associate judges.
Simon Waghorn of Astrolabe and Clive Jones of Nautilus received Wine Marlborough Lifetime Achievement Awards at the show.

CULTURE.head: Wine's cultural status slipping as alcohol sales fall and mocktails grow
CULTURE.summ: I was re-reading an article titled “Is Free Trade Passé?” that the economist Paul Krugman wrote back in 1987 and it got me thinking about what’s happening in the world today. Here is my report. >>><<< Is Free Trade Passé?
takeaways: Writer argues wine is less prominent at restaurant tables, with some venues offering longer mocktail lists than wine lists.
Writer says alcohol sales have fallen dramatically, using this to ask whether wine is passé as a social symbol.
Writer compares wine to coffee, which he says has become one option among many after the Starbucks and Dutch Bros. effect.

CULTURE.head: ASVO honours AWRI's Mark Krstic and Treasury's James Godfrey for industry service
CULTURE.summ: The Australian Society of Viticulture and Oenology (ASVO) celebrates the work of long-established wine career professionals. This year, AWRI’s Mark Krstic was honoured as the ASVO’s 31st ‘Fellow of the Society’ and Treasury Wine Estate’s James Godfrey was recognised through a newly created ‘Lifetime Acknowledgement Award’.
takeaways: The Australian Society of Viticulture and Oenology named AWRI managing director Dr Mark Krstic its 2026 Fellow of the Society.
Treasury Wine Estates winemaker James Godfrey received the society's new Lifetime Acknowledgement Award, especially for his work with fortified wines.
Godfrey has declared his recent retirement, and Krstic's AWRI tenure is drawing to a close.

CULTURE.head: Victorian Wine Show names Point Leo Estate Chardonnay Best Wine of Show
CULTURE.summ: The trophy winners for the 46th Annual Victorian Wine Show (VWS) have been announced with a “healthy mix of emerging smaller wineries and seasoned campaigners celebrating success”. The judging took place in Nagambie over three intensive days, with a total of 612 entries from 124 wineries. The annual show “recognises excellence...
takeaways: The 46th Victorian Wine Show, judged in Nagambie, handed out 21 trophies from 612 entries by 124 wineries.
Point Leo Estate's 2024 Reserve Chardonnay won Best Wine of Show, while Pfeiffer Wines was named Most Successful Exhibitor.
Hirsch Hill's La Chica con Tinta won Best Iberian Variety Wine with its first-ever 2026 Garnacha Blanca.

CULTURE.head: VinePair's Keith Beavers reflects on American wine in 2026
CULTURE.summ: This episode of Wine 101 is brought to you by Wines of Alsace and Alsace Rocks. Tucked between the Vosges Mountains and the Rhine River in northeastern France, Alsace is one of the most distinctive wine regions on earth, and is home to centuries of family winemaking, some of France’s most certifiably organic vineyards, and a...
takeaways: Keith Beavers, host of the VinePair podcast Wine 101, reflects on American wine in 2026.
The episode is sponsored by Wines of Alsace and Alsace Rocks.

CULTURE.head: Alison Smith Story recounts her path into the wine business
CULTURE.summ: This episode of Wine 101 is brought to you by Wines of Alsace and Alsace Rocks. Tucked between the Vosges Mountains and the Rhine River in northeastern France, Alsace is one of the most distinctive wine regions on earth, and is home to centuries of family winemaking, some of France’s most certifiably organic vineyards, and a...
takeaways: Alison Smith Story, of Smith Story Wine Cellars, tells her journey into wine on VinePair's Wine 101 podcast hosted by Keith Beavers.
The episode is a casual conversation about how Smith Story fell into the wine business.

SCIENCE.head: Burgundy estate uses electrical conductivity mapping to read vineyard soils
SCIENCE.summ: Electrical conductivity maps can reveal striking differences beneath seemingly uniform vineyards, but understanding what those differences mean is far more complicated
takeaways: Domaine du Cellier aux Moines in Givry, Burgundy, used electrical conductivity mapping from 2021 to guide soil pits.
Owner Philippe Pascal's 2026 trial found tressed Pinot Noir reached 13.6% potential alcohol versus 14.5% for trimmed vines.
A 2025 Médoc study linked electrical conductivity readings below about 50 centimeters to leaf nitrogen and water content.

SCIENCE.head: AWRI urges users to update its free agrochemical lookup app
SCIENCE.summ: 9 November 2026 The Australian Wine Research Institute has updated the version of the AWRI Agrochemical & MRL Search app on both the Apple App … more
takeaways: The Australian Wine Research Institute has released an updated version of its AWRI Agrochemical & MRL Search app.
The free app gives rapid access to information from the 'Agrochemicals registered for use in Australian viticulture' booklet.
Users on Apple App Store and Google Play Store are asked to update to keep receiving app updates.

NEWSLETTERS.head: 2024 was a remarkable year for Vintage Ports, as evidenced by these wines from the Symingtons
NEWSLETTERS.summ: I caught up with Charles and Harry Symington to taste through the remarkable Vintage Ports that they have
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jamie Goode
takeaways: Charles Symington says 2024 is the first general Vintage Port declaration in seven years, linked to climate change.
Symington's Warre 2024 Vintage Port is rated 95/100, while Dow 2024 is described as one of the driest wines at 99 g/l rs.
The Symingtons are increasingly using Sousão and Alicante Bouschet, with Alicante replacing Tinta Barocca in their Douro vineyards.

NEWSLETTERS.summ: Hello and welcome to my weekly roundup of the wine stories that I find of interest on the web. I

NEWSLETTERS.head: The Burgundy Region Quietly Absorbing This Year’s Rising Prices
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Discover how the Burgundy wine market quietly absorbs rising prices in 2026, revealing new trends and steady demand for fine wine collectors
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jonathan Finch
takeaways: Comité des Vins de Bourgogne figures show Burgundy white wine sales rose 0.4 per cent in the year to July 2026, while red fell 4.9 per cent.
Mâconnais bulk prices fell 9 per cent for Mâcon-Villages Blanc and 13 per cent for Bourgogne Blanc, per Burgundy wine board figures reported in March.
Pouilly-Fuissé was valued at about €817 a hectolitre for the 2024 harvest, versus roughly €3,050 for Puligny-Montrachet.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Choosing Thanksgiving Wines
NEWSLETTERS.summ: No single wine pairs perfectly with the Thanksgiving meal, but many styles can shine on your table
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Meg Maker recommends Chardonnay, off-dry Riesling, Pinot Noir, Gamay-based Beaujolais and sparkling wines as traditional Thanksgiving pairings.
She advises keeping wines at or below 13% alcohol, preferably 12.5%, so diners stay alert, especially at midday meals.
Maker suggests Champagne as the classic sparkling pick, with Crémant, Italian Método classico and Lambrusco as alternatives.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Five Minutes with... Rick Rainey & Léana Godard of Forge Cellars
NEWSLETTERS.summ: On Cabernet Franc’s untapped potential, giving Finger Lakes terroir a seat at the table, and why it’s all about joy
NEWSLETTERS.author: Cab Franc Chronicles
takeaways: Forge Cellars, established in 2011 on Seneca Lake in New York's Finger Lakes, began Cabernet Franc with its 2019 vintage.
Forge now makes four single-vineyard Cabernet Francs from different soils, including Willow (sand), Railroad (gravel), Arlo (clay) and Bellows (sand and rock).
In 2023 Forge left stems out entirely to understand each terroir's tannin potential, then reintroduced stems in some wines in 2024.

NEWSLETTERS.head: The Many Sins Of Wine Critics
NEWSLETTERS.summ: In the exciting (other adjectives are available) times we’re living in, we’re often told that writing is passé, people just don’t bother reading words anymore. A few journalistic outlets, especially in the financial press, seem to have finally come clean about the seriousness of their reporting, by auto-summarising their pieces...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: Tim Atkin argues wine critics should be only slightly more knowledgeable than their target audience, not vastly more expert.
Atkin says the American critic model favours tasting prowess, while the British model favours thoroughness and scholarship.
Atkin criticises the short time critics spend assessing wine, often about 30 seconds per sample, sometimes across dozens of wines in one session.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Find Rare Shizz With Orpheus Alerts!
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Some (more!) exciting news, folks: As many of you already know, sometimes wines get featured on here that are pretty rare. I’m talking about the kind of stuff that either doesn’t make it to the big platforms, or, if it does, is either priced astronomically or is gone in milliseconds. Understandably, that can be somewhat […]...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Joe Roberts
takeaways: 1WineDude is partnering with Orpheus Alerts, part of Orpheus Intelligence Labs Inc., to help buyers find rare wines.
Orpheus monitors sources like local-language catalogues, merchant inventory, auction and consignment notices, and restaurant or estate sales.
Users create alerts using natural-language descriptions or images, and Orpheus notifies them when matching wine is available and connects them with sellers.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Catalonia’s Under(wine)world
NEWSLETTERS.summ: How a Champagne trip in the 1800s resulted in a new Spanish wine in a league of its own
NEWSLETTERS.author: Eveline Chartier
takeaways: Josep Raventós of Penedès produced Spain's first traditional method sparkling wine in 1872, using Spanish indigenous grapes rather than Champagne varieties.
Cava gets its name from the Spanish word for cave or cellar, with underground cellars in Sant Sadurní d'Anoia reaching 20 m deep.
Sumarroca's 2022 Gran Reserva Brut Nature Cava, from Macabeu, Xarel•lo and Parellada, aged 40 months and sells for $28 Cdn.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Roadshow Review: Spain Brings Value Wines to China
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Does any nation offer better wine value than Spain? This seems obvious to French bottlers, who import major amounts of Spanish wine each year. Per
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jim Boyce
takeaways: The Wines From Castilla, La Mancha Roadshow stopped in Beijing, with a Guangzhou stop set for November 6.
Spain ranked fifth in China by volume last year, narrowly behind Italy, but only a quarter of leader Australia.
Spain ranked sixth by value in China, below New Zealand, with per-liter value only above Chile among the top eight sources.
